title: HelioPath POC bench sync: tripartite latency & throughput review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency and throughput benchmarks vs incumbent, discuss tuning (quant, routing, cache) and decide next test matrix. Redwood shows p99 latency improvement and higher sustained RPS under burst; customer concerned about long-tail and VPC egress costs.
next_steps: Priya to run 4k-token tail-latency run on dedicated cluster and share logs by 2027-05-03
Evan to send updated committed-slot pricing matrix and slot availability by 2027-05-01
HelioPath to share 2 anonymized query batches (50k tokens total) for KV/cache rewarm tests by 2027-04-30
action_items: Priya Desai: run 4k token tail-latency test on quantized model; due 2027-05-03
Evan Porter: prepare pricing + slot availability spreadsheet; due 2027-05-01
Jonas Fong: deliver anonymized query samples and top-20 conversation patterns; due 2027-04-30
Carlos Rivera: confirm VPC peering window and egress baseline (current provider) ; due 2027-05-02
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Evan, Priya (Redwood); Maya, Jonas, Carlos (HelioPath)

Summary (auto if present): quick numbers readout, triage of long-tail p99, routing fallback plan discussed, next-step owners assigned.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Evan from Redwood, I'll kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: Maya Lin here, hello.
[00:10] Jonas: Jonas, hi.
[00:12] Carlos: Carlos on the infra side.
[00:15] Priya: Priya Desai from Redwood, SE. Good to be here.

[00:23] Evan: Agenda is short — we're going to walk through the latest bench numbers we ran last night against your baseline, show where caching and quant helped, surface any anomalies, and then agree a short list of follow-ups.
[00:38] Maya: Perfect, Marco? sorry I mean Evan, please go ahead.
[00:41] Evan: (laughs) No Marco today. Okay, Priya, you want to share the screen?
[00:45] Priya: yes, sharing. So first slide — overall numbers. We tested three modes: Redwood hosted (standard), Redwood dedicated (reserved slots with bigger batch window), and your current vendor benchmark.
[01:05] Priya: p50s are pretty close across all, we've got p50 of 32ms on Redwood dedicated, 38ms on hosted, and 44ms on incumbent. p95 is where delta appears: 85ms dedicated, 120ms hosted, incumbent at 210ms. p99 is the big story — 115ms dedicated, 220ms hosted, incumbent 420ms. Those p99 numbers are median of three runs.
[01:34] Jonas: Whoa, incumbent p99 420ms? that seems high for our conversational path.
[01:39] Priya: Right, remember our test had some heavier context windows — the incumbent deferred to CPU fallback during cache churn, that spiked long tail.
[01:48] Carlos: Are these token-limited numbers or request-limited? want to map to our real traffic.
[01:51] Priya: Good question — these runs were 512-token average responses, mixed prompt lengths. We also did a 2k token run earlier that I'll show later.

[02:05] Evan: Also throughput: sustained RPS on dedicated slot pool was 420 rps with 512 tokens average (using continuous batching), hosted was 310 rps, incumbent plateaued at 190 rps before queuing. Tokens/sec roughly 215k for dedicated, 160k hosted, incumbent 95k.
[02:28] Maya: That throughput difference is promising. What's the hardware difference?
[02:31] Priya: Dedicated used A100-similar instance cluster with 8-card pool and optimized kernels; hosted was mixed clean-room instances with multi-tenant constraints; incumbent was on older Gen2 accelerators. Also our runtime chooses kernels based on sequence length distribution which helps.
[02:50] Jonas: Any special quantization? we saw notes about q4_0 and q8.
[02:54] Priya: For these runs the dedicated was q4_0 with KV cache warm, hosted used auto-quant profile (mix of q4_1 in some shards). Incumbent was FP16. The quant helped throughput and reduced memory pressure enabling larger batch windows.
[03:10] Carlos: But quant introduces some quality drift — did you do the eval on our prompt set?
[03:14] Priya: Yes we ran your 200 prompt eval — delta in BLEU-style and token-level similarity was <1.5% on q4_0 vs FP16 for the majority of queries; a handful of hallucination cases were flagged, we can share the diff set.

[03:33] Evan: Now the anomaly — the long tail on a subset of runs. We saw intermittent p99 spikes around 1.2s in hosted runs when cache eviction coincided with a burst. We suspect prefix-KV cold misses + backend GC in incumbent as cause.
[03:49] Jonas: That matches the logs we saw in our vendor tests; when a cold rewarm occurs it's catastrophic. How do you mitigate that?
[03:56] Priya: Two levers — proactive cache rewarm for hot prefixes and a fallback routing policy that sends requests to a spare capacity pool rather than letting a single node block. We demoed this in the last sprint but not enabled in these numbers.
[04:10] Maya: Can we see a run with rewarm enabled? the cold misses are our main concern for SLA.
[04:14] Priya: Absolutely — that's one of the next tests Priya will run (note: laughter). We'll do a 4k tok tail-latency run with rewarm and fallback enabled.

[04:30] Evan: I want to highlight unit economics too — token cost per 1M tokens on dedicated commitment drops ~38% vs hosted; incumbent list price was lower per token but their effective cost becomes higher when you account for slowdown and retry overhead.
[04:48] Carlos: Any visibility into network egress? we operate in VPC and egress to cloud endpoints is a line item.
[04:54] Priya: If you go Private (VPC peered) with Redwood Private we can reduce egress with regional placement and peering; for hosted we can provide estimates of egress between regions. We'll capture a delta in the pricing sheet Evan will send.

[05:10] Jonas: Security checklist — SOC2? audit logs? KMS?
[05:14] Evan: We have SOC 2 Type II coverage; Private offers customer-managed KMS and audit logs with retention options. We'll attach the security deck and the SOC 2 summary after the call.

[05:28] Maya: Great. Back to the metric — can you explain the batch sizing heuristics? how do you pick batch window without blowing latency?
[05:36] Priya: We use adaptive batching heuristics that expand window when utilization is low and shrink under tail pressure; dedicated slots allow a slightly larger batch window because resources are isolated. Also we do continuous KV streaming which keeps token gen path warm.
[05:49] Jonas: Sounds good. In your 2k token test you mentioned earlier— show that please.

[06:00] Priya: 2k-token runs: p50 110ms dedicated, p95 260ms dedicated, p99 430ms dedicated; hosted p99 hit 870ms and incumbent hit 1.6s. Note the absolute numbers go up with longer context, but the ratio vs incumbent remains favorable.
[06:20] Maya: Those longer tails still worry product. Do you have examples of worst-case traces?
[06:25] Priya: Yes attaching a few traces — in the worst cases you see a cold disk fallback or a swap event on incumbent node. On Redwood, spike traces correlate to cache eviction windows which we can control.
[06:40] Jonas: Can Redwood guarantee throttling or graceful degradation? our SLAs expect a soft cap.
[06:45] Evan: Yes we have automatic fallback to a smaller model variant or queue shaping; plus routing policies to divert traffic to dedicated spare lanes during pressure windows. That's in the rollout playbook.

[07:00] Maya: About fallback, what's the quality delta on fallback model? we need to know if fallback is acceptable for UX gracefully.
[07:05] Priya: Fallback is typically a trimmed param model or lower-precision quant. In our tests the fallback reduced token-level entropy by ~3%, and for 92% of conversational prompts users didn't notice major downstream differences. We'll include the comparison artifacts.

[07:22] Jonas: Ok, operationally — if we sign for dedicated slots, how long to provision?
[07:26] Evan: Typical lead time is 3-7 business days to provision dedicated pool after contract and payment clears; private/VPC setup can add 2-3 weeks depending on network approvals.

[07:40] Carlos: Are you able to run tests inside our VPC or do we have to replicate traffic to your hosted lab?
[07:46] Priya: We can run both. For Private deployments we can spin an evaluation cluster in your VPC under a time-limited eval. For hosted/dedicated we'll also do lab runs that mimic your traffic.

[08:00] Evan: Let's move to the special 'tripartite' test we ran — that is, routing between dedicated, hosted fallback, and incumbent for the handoff scenario, to measure end-to-end SLA under degradation.
[08:13] Priya: In that test we injected node-level failures on one dedicated card during a 10k rps ramp. Redwood continued to serve at 78% capacity with latency degradation of 1.2x p95; incumbent fell below 40% and queued requests.
[08:27] Jonas: Can you share the logs?
[08:30] Priya: yes will attach. There was a subtle config typo in one of the earlier runs — 're-route' policy accidentally set to 'best-effort' so we re-ran. The numbers I'm quoting are from the corrected runs.

[08:45] Maya: Nice. Are there any cases where Redwood lost tokens or produced truncated output under load?
[08:50] Priya: We did see a few truncations in hosted runs when we hit the per-tenant rate limiter, that's why we recommend dedicated for production traffic. Those truncations were absent in dedicated runs.

[09:05] Jonas: Anything on cold-start for KV cache on multi-tenant systems? you mentioned rewarm.
[09:09] Priya: We support prefix-based prefetch and asynchronous rewarm; for your top-200 prefixes prefetch reduced cold penalties by ~60%. We'll tune for your prefix distribution.

[09:22] Carlos: For the rewarm test, will it add cost? i.e., background compute costs?
[09:26] Priya: There's a modest compute cost for rewarm but it's small compared to retry/latency costs — we'll quantify that in the next cost delta sheet.

[09:40] (Short pause while Priya pulls up the 4k run)
[10:00] Priya: Alright here's the 4k-run summary — dedicated p95 520ms, p99 1.1s (with KV warm), hosted p99 2.6s, incumbent p99 ~3.8s. Important to stress these are mixed prompt types.
[10:18] Maya: 1.1s p99 still high for interactive UI, but much better than incumbent. Could we aim for p99 < 800ms?
[10:25] Priya: Possibly with more aggressive prefetch and smaller max-batch window for very long prompts; there's a tradeoff with throughput. We can try a tuned run.

[10:40] Jonas: Are queuing delays visible in the traces or just compute?
[10:44] Priya: Both — some spikes are from queue wait. Dedicated isolates that by spreading work across more slots and aggressive batching.

[10:55] Evan: Quick question — your current SLA threshold for interactive latency is what?
[10:58] Maya: We're targeting 800ms p99 for 95% of user-facing flows, and up to 1.5s allowed for heavier analytic flows.
[11:08] Evan: Noted. We'll try to hit that 800ms sweet spot on the next tuning pass.

[11:20] (Background noise, someone shuffling papers)
[11:30] Maya: Another operational question — how do you surface postmortems and alerts?
[11:34] Priya: We integrate with your monitoring via webhook and can send structured traces to your S3 or Elasticsearch, and we provide per-route alerting and automatic incident notes.

[11:46] Jonas: On the cost side can you break down committed slot economics vs on-demand?
[11:50] Evan: Committed slot gives ~30-45% discount depending on term and utilization. On-demand is higher but flexible. We'll detail numbers in the spreadsheet.

[12:05] Carlos: Any known limitations for our model family? we run a custom fine-tuned variant on top of the base.
[12:10] Priya: We onboarded several fine-tuned variants; memory grows with adapters but we've got a deployment pattern — sharded weights + quant helps. We might need to reserve extra memory per slot for your adapter set.

[12:26] Jonas: Can we do a head-to-head generate quality A/B during the same run to compare outputs?
[12:30] Priya: Yes we can run parallel generate-calls and store outputs for diff scoring. We'll add that to the next run matrix.

[12:45] Maya: Ok, earlier you mentioned fallback to a smaller variant; can we pick which prompts get fallback?
[12:51] Priya: Yes we can route by route-id or prefix rules; e.g., high-priority user flows pinned to dedicated only, analytic bulk lanes to fallback.

[13:04] Jonas: Great. On the action item about anonymized samples — is there a required format?
[13:08] Priya: CSV with prompt, expected tokens, and an anonymized user id is fine, 50k tokens across files works. We'll provide a template.

[13:20] Maya: We will try to hand that over by Friday.

[13:25] (Timestamp jump in transcript — people speaking over each other)
[13:30] Evan: Quick recap of numbers then: dedicated shows ~2x throughput vs incumbent and p99 improvements of ~3-4x in many tests, but long-tail on very long prompts still needs tuning.
[13:42] Jonas: Can you quantify retry overhead if we stick with incumbent? we've seen CPU thrash causing retries.
[13:48] Priya: In our traces retries added 12-18% extra token cost due to replays and client retries, and that doesn't count lost revenue from poor UX.

[14:00] Maya: Any regulatory constraints — data residency? we have EU customers.
[14:04] Evan: We can provision regional clusters and support private deployments in EU regions; Private gives more control for residency.

[14:16] Carlos: Another thing — do you instrument per-tenant throttling? we need fair-share on multitenant hosted.
[14:21] Priya: Yes per-tenant quotas, rate limits and token-level billing.

[14:30] (Priya shares a latency waterfall trace)
[14:45] Priya: This waterfall shows a cache miss event at 0.8s that propagates. If we prewarm top prefixes you can see p99 drops by ~60%.

[15:00] Jonas: Good. If prewarm helps that much it's probably worth the small extra cost.

[15:08] Maya: Are there any known bugs or regressions in this release?
[15:12] Priya: There was a bug in an autoscaler path that caused a small window of underprovisioning at very short sudden burst patterns; that was patched last week and not present in these results.

[15:26] Evan: Alright, let's agree the next test matrix: 1) 4k token tail-latency with prewarm & fallback enabled, 2) head-to-head A/B generate of 5k prompts, 3) VPC-provision cost estimate. Priya, will you own (1) and (2)?
[15:40] Priya: Yes will own and run in the lab and in a limited VPC eval if needed.
[15:45] Jonas: I'll own sample delivery for (2) and the prefixes for prewarm.

[15:52] Evan: Timelines — Priya by May 3 for tests; Evan will send pricing by May 1. Jonas and Carlos will confirm peering dates by May 2.

[16:05] Maya: Anything else on the bench itself?
[16:08] Priya: One last note — we saw a small noise band in hosted runs correlated to noisy neighbors; dedicated removes that, and Private gives the strongest isolation.

[16:20] (short silence)
[16:25] Carlos: Quick Q: can we get synthetic generator to replay traffic shape?
[16:29] Priya: Yes we can supply a load-replay harness with the same distribution as your traces.

[16:36] Evan: We'll also include a playbook doc for routing thresholds and fallback knobs.

[16:42] Maya: Thanks. Let's close with next steps recap.
[16:46] Evan: Recap: Priya runs 4k prewarm + fallback tests; Evan to send pricing; Jonas deliver samples; Carlos confirm peering windows. Any blockers?
[16:58] Jonas: none.
[17:00] Maya: none, thanks.
[17:02] Priya: I'll post logs and traces and the run artifacts to the shared folder.
[17:06] Evan: Great meeting — we'll follow up in Asana and email.
[17:10] (call starts to wrap; people say thanks)
[17:20] -- End of recorded transcript (some timestamps approximate, transcript auto-generated; a few words may be mis-heard, e.g., "re-route" transcribed as "reroot").
